payload.text: # Common Medications and Medical Conditions Guide ## Overview This guide provides evidence-based information about common medications and medical conditions. Always consult a qualified healthcare provider before starting, stopping, or changing any medication. --- ## Pain and Fever Medications ### Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) **Brand Names**: Tylenol, Panadol, Calpol **Uses**: - Relieve mild to moderate pain (headaches, toothaches, muscle aches) - Reduce fever **Dosage**: - Adults: 500-1000mg every 4-6 hours, maximum 4000mg per day - Children: Based on weight, usually 10-15mg/kg every 4-6 hours **Side Effects**: - Rare at recommended doses - Overdose can cause liver damage **Warnings**: - Do not take more than 4000mg in 24 hours - Avoid alcohol while taking paracetamol - Check other medications for paracetamol to avoid accidental overdose ### Ibuprofen **Brand Names**: Advil, Motrin, Nurofen **Uses**: - Relieve pain and inflammation (arthritis, sprains, headaches) - Reduce fever **Dosage**: - Adults: 200-400mg every 4-6 hours, maximum 1200mg per day **Side Effects**: - Stomach pain or indigestion - Nausea - Dizziness **Warnings**: - Take with food or milk to reduce stomach upset - Long-term use can increase risk of heart attack or stroke - Not recommended for people with stomach ulcers, kidney problems, or heart disease ### Aspirin **Brand Names**: Bayer, Ecotrin **Uses**: - Relieve pain and inflammation - Reduce fever - Low-dose (75-100mg daily) for heart attack and stroke prevention in at-risk individuals **Dosage**: - Pain relief: 325-650mg every 4-6 hours - Heart health: 75-100mg once daily (only as directed by doctor) **Side Effects**: - Stomach irritation - Increased risk of bleeding **Warnings**: - Do not give to children or teenagers (risk of Reye's syndrome) - Avoid with blood thinners unless directed by doctor --- ## Allergy Medications ### Cetirizine **Brand Names**: Zyrtec, Reactine **Uses**: - Relieve hay fever symptoms (sneezing, runny nose, itchy eyes) - Relieve allergic skin reactions (hives, itching) **Dosage**: - Adults and children over 12: 10mg once daily - Children 6-12: 5-10mg once daily **Side Effects**: - Drowsiness (less than older antihistamines) - Dry mouth - Headache **Warnings**: - May cause drowsiness in some people; avoid driving until you know how it affects you - Avoid alcohol ### Loratadine **Brand Names**: Claritin, Alavert **Uses**: - Relieve hay fever symptoms - Relieve hives and itching **Dosage**: - Adults and children over 6: 10mg once daily **Side Effects**: - Headache - Dry mouth - Fatigue **Warnings**: - Generally non-drowsy at recommended doses --- ## Heartburn and Acid Reflux Medications ### Omeprazole **Brand Names**: Prilosec, Losec **Uses**: - Treat heartburn and acid reflux - Treat and prevent stomach and duodenal ulcers - Treat GERD (Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease) **Dosage**: - Heartburn: 20mg once daily for 4-8 weeks - Maintenance: 20mg once daily or 10mg once daily **Side Effects**: - Headache - Stomach pain - Nausea - Diarrhea **Warnings**: - Long-term use (over 1 year) may increase risk of bone fractures, C. difficile infection, or low magnesium - Take 30-60 minutes before food ### Ranitidine **Brand Names**: Zantac **Uses**: - Relieve heartburn and indigestion - Treat and prevent ulcers **Note**: Many brands have been withdrawn due to potential contamination **Side Effects**: - Headache - Dizziness - Constipation or diarrhea --- ## High Blood Pressure Medications ### Amlodipine **Brand Names**: Norvasc **Uses**: - Treat high blood pressure (hypertension) - Treat angina (chest pain) **Dosage**: - Adults: 5-10mg once daily **Side Effects**: - Swelling of ankles or feet - Dizziness - Headache - Fatigue **Warnings**: - May cause dizziness when standing up quickly (orthostatic hypotension) ### Lisinopril **Brand Names**: Zestril, Prinivil **Uses**: - Treat high blood pressure - Treat heart failure - Improve survival after heart attack **Dosage**: - Hypertension: 10-40mg once daily **Side Effects**: - Dry cough (common) - Dizziness - Headache - High potassium levels **Warnings**: - Do not take if pregnant or breastfeeding - May cause allergic reactions (rare but serious) --- ## Diabetes Medications ### Metformin **Brand Names**: Glucophage, Glumetza **Uses**: - Treat type 2 diabetes - First-line treatment for type 2 diabetes **Dosage**: - 500mg twice daily or 850mg once daily, gradually increased as needed **Side Effects**: - Stomach upset (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea) - Metallic taste in mouth **Warnings**: - Take with food to reduce stomach upset - Rare but serious risk of lactic acidosis (seek medical help immediately if you have muscle pain, trouble breathing, or unusual tiredness) ### Insulin **Uses**: - Treat type 1 diabetes - Treat type 2 diabetes when other medications aren't enough **Types**: - Rapid-acting (insulin aspart, insulin lispro) - Short-acting (regular insulin) - Intermediate-acting (NPH insulin) - Long-acting (insulin glargine, insulin detemir) **Side Effects**: - Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) – symptoms include shaking, sweating, hunger, confusion, dizziness - Injection site reactions **Warnings**: - Learn to recognize and treat low blood sugar immediately - Always check blood sugar levels regularly - Rotate injection sites --- ## Antibiotics ### Amoxicillin **Brand Names**: Amoxil **Uses**: - Treat bacterial infections (ear infections, sinus infections, pneumonia, urinary tract infections) **Dosage**: - Adults: 250-500mg every 8 hours or 500-875mg every 12 hours **Side Effects**: - Nausea - Vomiting - Diarrhea - Rash **Warnings**: - Complete the full course even if you feel better - May reduce effectiveness of birth control pills - Do not take if allergic to penicillin ### Azithromycin **Brand Names**: Zithromax **Uses**: - Treat bacterial infections (chest infections, ear infections, skin infections) - Single-dose option for some infections **Dosage**: - 500mg once daily for 3-5 days **Side Effects**: - Stomach upset - Nausea - Diarrhea - Headache **Warnings**: - Take on empty stomach for better absorption - May cause heart rhythm problems in rare cases --- ## Mental Health Medications ### Sertraline **Brand Names**: Zoloft **Uses**: - Treat depression - Treat anxiety disorders (GAD, OCD, panic disorder, PTSD) - Treat social anxiety disorder **Dosage**: - Depression/anxiety: 50-200mg once daily **Side Effects**: - Nausea - Headache - Insomnia or drowsiness - Sexual side effects - Weight changes **Warnings**: - May take 4-6 weeks to feel full effect - Do not stop suddenly (risk of withdrawal symptoms) - Increased risk of suicidal thoughts in young adults (monitor closely) ### Fluoxetine **Brand Names**: Prozac **Uses**: - Treat depression - Treat OCD - Treat bulimia nervosa - Treat panic disorder **Dosage**: - Depression: 20-80mg once daily **Side Effects**: - Nausea - Headache - Insomnia - Sexual side effects **Warnings**: - Same as sertraline --- ## Common Medical Conditions ### Fever **What is it?**: Elevated body temperature, usually above 38°C (100.4°F) **Causes**: - Infections (viral or bacterial) - Inflammatory conditions - Vaccinations **Home Care**: - Stay hydrated - Rest - Paracetamol or ibuprofen (if appropriate) to reduce fever and discomfort **When to see a doctor**: - Fever in infants under 3 months - Fever over 40°C (104°F) - Fever lasting more than 3 days in children or 5 days in adults - Symptoms like difficulty breathing, chest pain, confusion, stiff neck ### Headache **Types**: 1. Tension-type headaches (most common) 2. Migraines 3. Cluster headaches (rare) **Home Care**: - Rest in dark, quiet room - Paracetamol or ibuprofen - Drink water (dehydration is common cause) **When to see a doctor**: - Sudden, severe headache ("worst ever") - Headache with fever, stiff neck, confusion, weakness, vision changes - Headache after head injury - Frequent or worsening headaches ### Common Cold **Causes**: Viral infection (rhinovirus most common) **Symptoms**: - Runny or stuffy nose - Sore throat - Cough - Mild fever - Fatigue **Treatment**: - No cure; symptoms usually last 7-10 days - Rest - Stay hydrated - Paracetamol or ibuprofen for pain/fever - Warm drinks and honey (for cough in children over 1) **When to see a doctor**: - Symptoms last more than 10 days - Fever lasts more than 3 days - Difficulty breathing - Chest pain - Severe sore throat with fever (possible strep throat) ### High Blood Pressure (Hypertension) **What is it?**: Pressure in arteries is consistently too high **Symptoms**: Often no symptoms ("silent killer") **Complications if untreated**: - Heart attack - Stroke - Kidney disease - Eye problems **Management**: - Healthy diet (low salt, plenty of fruits/vegetables) - Regular exercise - Maintain healthy weight - Reduce stress - Medications (if lifestyle changes not enough) ### Type 2 Diabetes **What is it?**: Body doesn't use insulin properly or doesn't make enough insulin **Symptoms**: - Increased thirst and hunger - Frequent urination - Fatigue - Blurred vision - Slow-healing sores **Management**: - Healthy diet - Regular exercise - Weight management - Medications or insulin (as directed) - Regular blood sugar monitoring ### Asthma **What is it?**: Chronic condition affecting airways, causing wheezing, breathlessness, chest tightness **Triggers**: - Allergens (dust mites, pollen, pet dander) - Air pollution - Smoke - Exercise - Cold air - Viral infections **Management**: - Avoid triggers - Inhaled corticosteroids (preventer) - Short-acting beta-agonists (reliever) - Follow asthma action plan from doctor --- ## General Guidelines - Always read and follow medication labels - Keep medications out of reach of children - Do not share medications with others - Store medications as directed (some need refrigeration, some need to be kept in dry places) - Keep a list of all medications you take (prescription and over-the-counter) to show doctors and pharmacists - Tell your doctor about all medications, supplements, and herbs you take to avoid interactions --- ## When to Seek Emergency Medical Help Call emergency services immediately if you experience: - Chest pain or pressure - Difficulty breathing or shortness of breath - Sudden numbness or weakness of face, arm, or leg (especially on one side) - Sudden confusion, trouble speaking or understanding - Sudden trouble seeing in one or both eyes - Sudden trouble walking, dizziness, loss of balance or coordination - Severe or persistent vomiting or diarrhea - Severe allergic reaction (hives, swelling of face/lips/tongue, difficulty breathing) - Bleeding that doesn't stop after 10 minutes of direct pressure - Loss of consciousness
